{"learner":"Level: true beginner in Spanish. Knows 'hola' and '¿Cómo estás?' only as memorized phrases.
Goal: conversation with Peruvian coworkers and a Peruvian client, so workplace language comes first.
Known gaps: me vs. mi, subject pronouns, ser vs. estar, verb endings, noun gender, and time words (hoy vs. mañana).
Strengths: fluent in English, Gujarati, and Hindi, so grammar contrasts and cognates will help.","must_fix":["Wrote 'Mi llamo'; the correct form is 'Me llamo' (reflexive 'me', not possessive 'mi').","Wrote English 'work'; the Spanish word is 'trabajo'.","Wrote 'estu', which is not a Spanish word; needs a form of 'ser' (es) or 'estar' (está).","Confused 'mañana' (tomorrow) with 'hoy' (today)."],"lessons":[{"id":"me-llamo-soy","title":"Introducing Yourself","objective":"Introduce yourself by name and origin in one or two sentences, and respond to 'Mucho gusto'.","teach_notes":"Start from their 'Mi llamo' attempt. Contrast 'mi' (my) with 'me' (myself) using their own name. Have them say 'Me llamo Alex' aloud several times before adding origin.","key_facts":["'Me llamo' + name means 'My name is' + name.","'Mi' means 'my' and cannot replace 'me' in 'me llamo'.","'Soy de' + place means 'I am from' + place.","'Mucho gusto' means 'Nice to meet you.'"],"fixes":["Wrote 'Mi llamo' instead of 'Me llamo'."]},{"id":"subject-pronouns-ser","title":"Subject Pronouns and Ser","objective":"Say who someone is using yo, tú, usted, él, and ella with the forms soy, eres, and es.","teach_notes":"Compare with English 'I am / you are', which they already know. Stress that Spanish verb endings often show the subject, so pronouns are frequently dropped. Practice with coworker names.","key_facts":["'Yo soy' means 'I am'.","'Tú eres' means 'you (informal) are'.","'Usted es' means 'you (formal) are'.","'Ser' conjugates as soy, eres, es, somos, son.","Subject pronouns are often omitted because the verb ending shows the subject."],"fixes":[]},{"id":"trabajo-occupations","title":"Talking About Your Job","objective":"Describe your job, workplace, and employer using 'trabajo' and 'Trabajo para'.","teach_notes":"Replace their English 'work' with 'trabajo' by showing it as both noun and verb. Build sentences from their own job. Use 'Trabajo como' to introduce profession and 'Trabajo para' for the client.","key_facts":["'Trabajo' means both 'I work' and 'job/work' (noun).","'Trabajo como' + profession means 'I work as a' + profession.","'Trabajo en' + place means 'I work at' + place.","'Trabajo para' + company means 'I work for' + company.","'Mi trabajo es' means 'My job is'."],"fixes":["Wrote English 'work' instead of 'trabajo'."]},{"id":"estar-como-estas","title":"Estar and Asking How People Are","objective":"Ask and answer how someone is, and say where you are, using estoy, estás, and está.","teach_notes":"Revisit '¿Cómo estás?' so they see the verb behind it. Contrast 'soy' (identity) with 'estoy' (state, location). Their 'estu' attempt shows they need this contrast.","key_facts":["'Estar' conjugates as estoy, estás, está, estamos, están.","'¿Cómo estás?' is informal; '¿Cómo está usted?' is formal.","'Estar' is used for temporary states and location, as in 'Estoy en Lima'.","'Soy ingeniero' uses 'ser' for profession, while 'Estoy cansado' uses 'estar' for state."],"fixes":["Wrote 'estu', which is not a Spanish word; should be 'estoy', 'está', or 'es'."]},{"id":"gender-articles","title":"Noun Gender and Articles","objective":"Use el, la, un, and una correctly with common workplace nouns.","teach_notes":"Connect gender to their Gujarati and Hindi experience, where gender agreement also exists. Teach with workplace nouns they will actually use. Emphasize that -o endings are usually masculine and -a usually feminine.","key_facts":["'El' means 'the' with masculine nouns; 'la' means 'the' with feminine nouns.","'Un' means 'a' with masculine nouns; 'una' means 'a' with feminine nouns.","Most nouns ending in -o are masculine, and most ending in -a are feminine.","'El trabajo' means 'the job'; 'la empresa' means 'the company'.","'El proyecto' means 'the project'."],"fixes":[]},{"id":"hoy-manana-ayer","title":"Time Words: Today, Tomorrow, Yesterday","objective":"Refer to today, tomorrow, and yesterday correctly in workplace sentences.","teach_notes":"Use a timeline on paper with yesterday, today, tomorrow. Point out that 'mañana' also means morning, so context matters. Have them check their own schedule aloud each day.","key_facts":["'Hoy' means 'today'.","'Mañana' means 'tomorrow'.","'Ayer' means 'yesterday'.","'La mañana' means 'the morning' and uses the same spelling as 'mañana' but a different meaning.","'Pasado mañana' means 'the day after tomorrow'."],"fixes":["Confused 'mañana' (tomorrow) with 'hoy' (today)."]},{"id":"present-tense-ar","title":"Regular -ar Verbs in the Present","objective":"Conjugate -ar verbs like trabajar and hablar in the present for yo, tú, usted, and ellos.","teach_notes":"Give the ending pattern first, then use 'trabajar' repeatedly in their real routine. Show that the same endings apply to any -ar verb. Keep examples personal and short.","key_facts":["-ar present endings are -o, -as, -a, -amos, and -an.","'Trabajar' conjugates as trabajo, trabajas, trabaja, trabajamos, trabajan.","'Hablar' means 'to speak' and conjugates as hablo, hablas, habla.","'Yo hablo español' means 'I speak Spanish'.","'Ellos trabajan' means 'they work'."],"fixes":[]},{"id":"question-words","title":"Asking Questions","objective":"Ask basic workplace questions using question words and correct question punctuation.","teach_notes":"Practice question words as a fixed set they can reuse. Point out that Spanish questions have an upside-down opening mark. Have them ask questions to a partner and answer them.","key_facts":["'¿Qué?' means 'what?'; '¿Dónde?' means 'where?'; '¿Cuándo?' means 'when?'.","'¿Cómo?' means 'how?'; '¿Por qué?' means 'why?'; '¿Quién?' means 'who?'.","Spanish questions begin with an upside-down question mark (¿) and end with (?).","'¿Dónde trabaja usted?' means 'Where do you work?' (formal)."],"fixes":[]},{"id":"usted-workplace-peru","title":"Formal and Informal You in Peru","objective":"Choose between usted and tú appropriately with clients, senior colleagues, and peers, and use basic polite phrases.","teach_notes":"Explain that usted signals respect and is standard with clients. Let them practice switching registers in role-play. Note that peers may invite them to use tú.","key_facts":["'Usted' (abbreviated 'Ud.') is the formal 'you'; 'tú' is the informal 'you'.","Use usted with clients and senior colleagues until invited to use tú.","'Disculpe' means 'excuse me' (formal); 'disculpa' is informal.","'Por favor' means 'please'; 'Muchas gracias' means 'thank you very much'."],"fixes":[]},{"id":"scheduling-meetings","title":"Scheduling Meetings","objective":"Propose and confirm a meeting day and time with a coworker or client.","teach_notes":"Build from their need: arranging calls with the Peruvian client. Practice a short exchange: propose, confirm, close. Reinforce 'mañana' versus 'hoy' within a realistic scheduling dialogue.","key_facts":["Days of the week are lunes, martes, miércoles, jueves, viernes, sábado, and domingo.","Days of the week are not capitalized in Spanish.","'¿Podemos reunirnos el jueves?' means 'Can we meet on Thursday?'","'A las tres' means 'at three o'clock'.","'Nos vemos mañana' means 'See you tomorrow'."],"fixes":[]}]}

{"explain":"Use 'me llamo' + your name to say 'My name is...'. Here 'me' means 'myself,' while 'mi' means 'my' and cannot replace it, so write 'Me llamo Alex,' not 'Mi llamo Alex.' To say where you're from, use 'soy de' + place: 'Soy de Londres' means 'I am from London.' When someone says 'Mucho gusto,' it means 'Nice to meet you,' so you can reply with the same words. Example: 'Me llamo Alex. Soy de Londres. Mucho gusto.'","items":[{"type":"mcq","q":"Which sentence means 'My name is Ana'?","options":["Me llamo Ana.","Mi llamo Ana.","Me llamas Ana.","Soy llamo Ana."],"answer":"Me llamo Ana.","why":"'Me llamo' + name means 'My name is' + name.","tests":0},{"type":"mcq","q":"Fill in the blank: '___ llamo Pedro.'","options":["Me","Mi","Mis","Mo"],"answer":"Me","why":"'Mi' means 'my' and cannot replace 'me' in 'me llamo'.","tests":1},{"type":"mcq","q":"Which sentence means 'I am from Lima'?","options":["Soy de Lima.","Estoy de Lima.","Soy en Lima.","Tengo Lima."],"answer":"Soy de Lima.","why":"'Soy de' + place means 'I am from' + place.","tests":2},{"type":"mcq","q":"What does 'Mucho gusto' mean?","options":["Nice to meet you.","See you later.","Thank you very much.","How are you?"],"answer":"Nice to meet you.","why":"'Mucho gusto' means 'Nice to meet you.'","tests":3},{"type":"recall","q":"Write the Spanish for 'My name is Carlos.'","answer":"Me llamo Carlos.","accept":["Me llamo Carlos","me llamo Carlos."],"why":"'Me llamo' + name means 'My name is' + name.","tests":0},{"type":"recall","q":"Write the Spanish for 'I am from Cusco.'","answer":"Soy de Cusco.","accept":["Soy de Cusco","soy de Cusco."],"why":"'Soy de' + place means 'I am from' + place.","tests":2}]}

{"explain":"Ser means 'to be' and is used to say who someone is. Learn these forms: soy (I am), eres (you informal are), es (he, she, or you formal are), somos (we are), son (they are). The subject pronouns are yo (I), tú (you informal), usted (you formal), él (he), and ella (she). Use usted with clients and people you have just met, and tú with friends. Example: 'Yo soy Rosa' means 'I am Rosa.' Spanish verb endings already show the subject, so the pronoun is often dropped: 'Soy Rosa' is natural. 'Él es Pedro' means 'He is Pedro.'","items":[{"type":"mcq","q":"What does 'Yo soy Rosa' mean?","options":["I am Rosa","You are Rosa","She is Rosa","We are Rosa"],"answer":"I am Rosa","why":"'Yo soy' means 'I am', so 'Yo soy Rosa' means 'I am Rosa'.","tests":0},{"type":"mcq","q":"Which sentence means 'You (informal) are an engineer'?","options":["Tú eres ingeniero","Usted es ingeniero","Yo soy ingeniero","Nosotros somos ingenieros"],"answer":"Tú eres ingeniero","why":"'Tú eres' means 'you (informal) are', and it is used with 'ingeniero'.","tests":1},{"type":"mcq","q":"Which is the polite way to ask a client 'Are you Mr. Torres?'","options":["¿Usted es el señor Torres?","¿Tú eres el señor Torres?","¿Yo soy el señor Torres?","¿Ella es el señor Torres?"],"answer":"¿Usted es el señor Torres?","why":"'Usted es' is the formal 'you are', which fits a client you have just met.","tests":2},{"type":"mcq","q":"Which form completes the sentence: 'Nosotros ___ de Lima.'?","options":["somos","son","soy","eres"],"answer":"somos","why":"'Nosotros' (we) takes 'somos', the 'we' form of ser.","tests":3},{"type":"recall","q":"Write the Spanish for 'I am Ana,' leaving out the subject pronoun.","answer":"Soy Ana.","accept":["Soy Ana"],"why":"The verb ending 'soy' already shows the subject 'I', so 'yo' is usually dropped.","tests":4},{"type":"recall","q":"Write the Spanish for 'You (informal) are Lucía.'","answer":"Tú eres Lucía.","accept":["Eres Lucía.","Eres Lucía","Tú eres Lucía"],"why":"'Tú eres' means 'you (informal) are', and the pronoun 'tú' may be dropped.","tests":1}]}

{"explain":"'Trabajo' means both 'I work' (verb) and 'job/work' (noun). Use it in four patterns. 'Trabajo como' + profession = 'I work as a' + profession. 'Trabajo en' + place = 'I work at' + place. 'Trabajo para' + company = 'I work for' + company. 'Mi trabajo es' = 'My job is'. Example: 'Trabajo como ingeniero en Lima para Banco Andino. Mi trabajo es manejar proyectos.' Translation: 'I work as an engineer in Lima for Banco Andino. My job is managing projects.'","items":[{"type":"mcq","q":"Which word means 'I work' (the verb)?","options":["Trabajo","Trabajas","Trabajamos","Trabajan"],"answer":"Trabajo","why":"'Trabajo' is the 'yo' form of the verb, so it means 'I work', and it is also the noun 'job/work'.","tests":0},{"type":"mcq","q":"What does 'Trabajo como enfermera' mean?","options":["I work as a nurse","I work at a hospital","I work for a nurse","My job is a nurse"],"answer":"I work as a nurse","why":"'Trabajo como' followed by a profession means 'I work as a' + that profession.","tests":1},{"type":"mcq","q":"Which sentence means 'I work at a school'?","options":["Trabajo en una escuela","Trabajo para una escuela","Trabajo como una escuela","Mi trabajo es una escuela"],"answer":"Trabajo en una escuela","why":"'Trabajo en' followed by a place means 'I work at' that place.","tests":2},{"type":"mcq","q":"Which sentence means 'My job is teaching'?","options":["Mi trabajo es enseñar","Trabajo para enseñar","Mi trabajo en enseñar","Trabajo como enseñar"],"answer":"Mi trabajo es enseñar","why":"'Mi trabajo es' plus a verb or noun means 'My job is' that activity.","tests":4},{"type":"recall","q":"Write the Spanish for 'I work for Banco Andino.'","answer":"Trabajo para Banco Andino.","accept":["Trabajo para Banco Andino","trabajo para Banco Andino.","Trabajo para Banco Andino"],"why":"'Trabajo para' followed by a company name means 'I work for' that company.","tests":3},{"type":"recall","q":"Write the Spanish for 'I work as a teacher.'","answer":"Trabajo como profesor.","accept":["Trabajo como profesor","Trabajo como profesora.","Trabajo como profesora","trabajo como profesor."],"why":"'Trabajo como' plus a profession means 'I work as a' + profession; 'profesor' or 'profesora' depends on the speaker's gender.","tests":1}]}

{"explain":"Estar means 'to be' for states and locations. Its forms are estoy, estás, está, estamos, están. '¿Cómo estás?' is informal, used with friends and coworkers. '¿Cómo está usted?' is formal, used with clients you don't know well. Use estar for temporary states and location: 'Estoy en Lima' (I am in Lima), 'Estoy cansado' (I am tired). Use ser for identity and profession: 'Soy ingeniero' (I am an engineer). Your 'estu' was a mix-up: 'estoy' is the form for 'I'.","items":[{"type":"mcq","q":"Which form of estar goes with 'yo' (I)?","options":["estoy","estás","está","estamos"],"answer":"estoy","why":"'Yo' takes estoy, while estás is for tú and está is for él, ella, or usted.","tests":0},{"type":"mcq","q":"Which is the formal way to ask a client how they are?","options":["¿Cómo estás?","¿Cómo está usted?","¿Cómo estoy?","¿Cómo estamos?"],"answer":"¿Cómo está usted?","why":"Usted takes the está form, and the 'usted' makes the question formal.","tests":1},{"type":"mcq","q":"Which sentence correctly says 'I am in Lima'?","options":["Estoy en Lima","Soy en Lima","Estoy de Lima","Es en Lima"],"answer":"Estoy en Lima","why":"Location uses estar, so 'Estoy en Lima' is correct, while 'Soy de Lima' means 'I am from Lima'.","tests":2},{"type":"mcq","q":"Which sentence uses ser for a profession?","options":["Soy ingeniero","Estoy ingeniero","Soy cansado","Estoy cansado"],"answer":"Soy ingeniero","why":"Profession uses ser, so 'Soy ingeniero' is correct, while 'Estoy cansado' uses estar for a temporary state.","tests":3},{"type":"recall","q":"Write the form of estar that goes with 'tú' (informal you).","answer":"estás","accept":["Estás"],"why":"Tú takes estás, the informal form found in '¿Cómo estás?'.","tests":0},{"type":"recall","q":"Write the Spanish for 'I am tired' using estar.","answer":"Estoy cansado","accept":["Estoy cansada","estoy cansado","estoy cansada"],"why":"Tiredness is a temporary state, so it takes estar, and 'Estoy' is the 'I' form.","tests":2}]}

{"learner":"Level: absolute beginner, fluent in English, Gujarati and Hindi.
Goal: hold everyday workplace conversations with coworkers at a Peruvian client.
Knows: hola and como estas.
Gaps: confuses mi and me ('Mi llamo'), mixes English into sentences and invents verb forms ('Mi work estu').
Also confuses mañana with today and omits Spanish accents and ñ.","lessons":[{"id":"greetings","title":"Greet Coworkers at Any Time of Day","objective":"Greet a coworker appropriately for the time of day and ask how they are, spelling the question correctly.","explain":"Buenos días means good morning. Buenas tardes means good afternoon. Buenas noches means good evening or good night. ¿Cómo estás? asks a peer how they are. Cómo and estás both carry written accents. Spanish questions open with ¿ and close with ?. Example: at 3 p.m., say to a coworker, "Hola, buenas tardes. ¿Cómo estás?"","key_facts":["Buenos días means good morning.","Buenas tardes means good afternoon.","Buenas noches means good evening or good night.","¿Cómo estás? asks a peer how they are.","Cómo and estás both carry written accents.","Spanish questions open with ¿ and close with ?."],"fixes":["Wrote como estas without accents or question marks."],"items":[{"type":"mcq","q":"It is 9 a.m. Which greeting fits best?","options":["Buenas noches","Buenos días","Buenas tardes","Hasta mañana"],"answer":"Buenos días","why":"Buenos días means good morning.","tests":0},{"type":"mcq","q":"What does buenas tardes mean?","options":["Good morning","Good night","Good afternoon","Good day off"],"answer":"Good afternoon","why":"Tardes is the afternoon form used in this greeting.","tests":1},{"type":"mcq","q":"Which is written correctly?","options":["como estas?","¿Como estas?","¿Cómo estas?","¿Cómo estás?"],"answer":"¿Cómo estás?","why":"It needs both accents plus the opening and closing question marks.","tests":4},{"type":"mcq","q":"You are leaving work at 8 p.m. What can you say?","options":["Buenas noches","Buenos días","Buenas tardes","Buenos tardes"],"answer":"Buenas noches","why":"Buenas noches means good evening or good night.","tests":2},{"type":"recall","q":"Write the Spanish for 'How are you?' to a peer, with correct punctuation and accents.","answer":"¿Cómo estás?","accept":[],"why":"This is the peer question, with two accents and both question marks.","tests":3},{"type":"recall","q":"What punctuation mark opens a Spanish question?","answer":"¿","accept":["an upside-down question mark","an inverted question mark"],"why":"Spanish questions open with ¿ and close with ?.","tests":5}]},{"id":"my-name","title":"Say Your Name","objective":"Introduce yourself, ask a peer's name and respond politely when meeting someone.","explain":"Me llamo means my name is; literally, it means I call myself. Use me, not mi, in me llamo. Mi nombre es also means my name is, because mi means my and nombre means name. ¿Cómo te llamas? asks a peer's name. Mucho gusto means nice to meet you. Example: "Hola, me llamo Alex. Mucho gusto."","key_facts":["Me llamo means my name is; literally, it means I call myself.","Use me, not mi, in me llamo.","Mi nombre es also means my name is, because mi means my and nombre means name.","¿Cómo te llamas? asks a peer's name.","Mucho gusto means nice to meet you."],"fixes":["Wrote 'Mi llamo' instead of 'Me llamo'."],"items":[{"type":"mcq","q":"Which sentence is correct?","options":["Mi llamo Alex.","Me llamo Alex.","Me nombre Alex.","Mi llamas Alex."],"answer":"Me llamo Alex.","why":"The fixed phrase uses me, not mi.","tests":1},{"type":"mcq","q":"What is the literal meaning of me llamo?","options":["I know myself","You call me","I call myself","My call is"],"answer":"I call myself","why":"Me llamo literally means I call myself, though we translate it as my name is.","tests":0},{"type":"mcq","q":"Which sentence also correctly gives your name?","options":["Me nombre es Alex.","Mi nombre llamo Alex.","Me nombre llamo Alex.","Mi nombre es Alex."],"answer":"Mi nombre es Alex.","why":"Mi means my, so it goes with nombre.","tests":2},{"type":"mcq","q":"A new coworker tells you their name. What is a natural reply?","options":["Mucho gusto.","Buenas noches.","Me llamas.","Mi nombre."],"answer":"Mucho gusto.","why":"Mucho gusto means nice to meet you.","tests":4},{"type":"recall","q":"Ask a peer in Spanish: 'What is your name?'","answer":"¿Cómo te llamas?","accept":[],"why":"¿Cómo te llamas? is the peer question for someone's name.","tests":3},{"type":"recall","q":"Correct this sentence: 'Mi llamo Alex.'","answer":"Me llamo Alex.","accept":["Mi nombre es Alex."],"why":"Llamo needs me, while mi only works with a noun such as nombre.","tests":1}]},{"id":"tu-usted-ustedes","title":"Choose the Right 'You'","objective":"Choose tú, usted or ustedes to suit the person and workplace situation.","explain":"Tú is informal you for one person. Usted is respectful you for one person. Like Hindi aap, usted shows respect. Ustedes is you for a group in Peru, formal or casual. ¿Cómo está? is the usted form of ¿Cómo estás? Use usted with a client until invited to use tú. Example: to a new client, say, "Buenos días. ¿Cómo está usted?"","key_facts":["Tú is informal you for one person.","Usted is respectful you for one person.","Like Hindi aap, usted shows respect.","Ustedes is you for a group in Peru, formal or casual.","¿Cómo está? is the usted form of ¿Cómo estás?","Use usted with a client until invited to use tú."],"fixes":[],"items":[{"type":"mcq","q":"Which word is informal 'you' for one person?","options":["Ustedes","Usted","Tú","Mi"],"answer":"Tú","why":"Tú is the informal singular you.","tests":0},{"type":"mcq","q":"Which Spanish word is closest in respect to Hindi aap?","options":["Tú","Usted","Mi","Me"],"answer":"Usted","why":"Like aap, usted shows respect.","tests":2},{"type":"mcq","q":"You are addressing your whole team in Peru. Which word do you use?","options":["Ustedes","Tú","Usted","Me"],"answer":"Ustedes","why":"Ustedes is you for a group in Peru, formal or casual.","tests":3},{"type":"mcq","q":"You meet a client for the first time. What should you ask?","options":["¿Cómo estás tú?","¿Cómo te llamas tú?","¿Cómo estás?","¿Cómo está usted?"],"answer":"¿Cómo está usted?","why":"Use usted with a client until invited to use tú.","tests":5},{"type":"recall","q":"Change ¿Cómo estás? to the usted form.","answer":"¿Cómo está?","accept":["¿Cómo está usted?"],"why":"Está is the form that goes with usted.","tests":4},{"type":"recall","q":"Which Spanish word means respectful 'you' for one person?","answer":"Usted","accept":[],"why":"Usted is the respectful singular you.","tests":1}]},{"id":"ser-identity","title":"Say Who You Are and Where You're From","objective":"Use soy, eres and es to state identity and origin.","explain":"Soy means I am. Eres means you are, for tú. Es means he is, she is, or you are for usted. Soy de means I am from. Spanish usually drops yo, the word for I, because soy already shows who is meant. Example: "Soy Alex. Soy de India." Then ask a peer, "¿Eres de Lima?"","key_facts":["Soy means I am.","Eres means you are, for tú.","Es means he is, she is, or you are for usted.","Soy de means I am from.","Spanish usually drops yo, the word for I, because soy already shows who is meant."],"fixes":[],"items":[{"type":"mcq","q":"How do you say 'I am Alex'?","options":["Es Alex.","Eres Alex.","Soy Alex.","Mi Alex."],"answer":"Soy Alex.","why":"Soy means I am.","tests":0},{"type":"mcq","q":"Which form goes with tú?","options":["Eres","Soy","Es","Mi"],"answer":"Eres","why":"Eres means you are, for tú.","tests":1},{"type":"mcq","q":"Which form do you use to say 'you are' to a client addressed as usted?","options":["Soy","Eres","Estás","Es"],"answer":"Es","why":"Es covers he, she and usted.","tests":2},{"type":"mcq","q":"Which is the most natural everyday way to say 'I am from India'?","options":["Mi de India.","Soy de India.","Es de India.","Eres de India."],"answer":"Soy de India.","why":"Soy de means I am from, and yo is usually dropped.","tests":3},{"type":"recall","q":"What does yo mean, and why is it often dropped before soy?","answer":"Yo means I, and it is often dropped because soy already shows who is meant.","accept":["It means I; soy already shows the subject."],"why":"The verb form soy already points to the speaker.","tests":4},{"type":"recall","q":"Write in Spanish: 'I am from India.'","answer":"Soy de India.","accept":["Yo soy de India."],"why":"Soy de means I am from.","tests":3}]},{"id":"talking-about-work","title":"Talk About Your Work","objective":"Say what you do and who you work with in full Spanish sentences.","explain":"Trabajo means I work. Example: "Soy ingeniero. Trabajo con un cliente de Perú. Mi trabajo es interesante."","key_facts":["Trabajo means I work.","Trabajo also means job, so mi trabajo means my job.","Trabajo con means I work with.","Es, not estu, means is.","Use soy with no word for a before a job: soy ingeniero for a man, soy ingeniera for a woman."],"fixes":["Wrote 'Mi work estu', mixing the English word work into Spanish and using estu for is."],"items":[{"type":"mcq","q":"What is the Spanish for 'my job'?","options":["mi work","me trabajo","mi trabajo","me work"],"answer":"mi trabajo","why":"Trabajo means job, and mi means into full Spanish: 'Mi work estu interesante.'","answer":"Mi trabajo es interesante.","accept":[],"why":"Use trabajo for work or job and es for is.","tests":3}]},{"id":"hoy-manana-ayer","title":"Today, Tomorrow, Yesterday","objective":"Refer correctly to today, tomorrow, yesterday and the morning.","explain":"Hoy means today.
